newsitem.title: USA: Democrats urge military budget cut.
newsitem.headline: Democrats urge military budget cut.

text.p: More than 100 congressional Democrats urged President Clinton Friday to resist a budget deal that would keep military spending level, saying that would force steep non-defence programme cuts.

"We believe that the current military budget significantly exceeds what is required ... while important health, public safety, environmental, educational and other functions of the federal government will suffer greatly if Republican priorities are followed," they said in a letter circulated by Representative Barney Frank, a Massachusetts Democrat, and signed by 109 House Democrats.

The Republican-controlled Congress approved $10 billion more than Clinton requested for defence in 1996 and $7 billion more this year. Republican leaders asked the House and Senate budget committees to approve $268 billion for defence next year, saying they were willing to continue at this year's rate rather than seek further increases.
But Frank said in a brief interview that "that is unacceptable. If you keep defence level then everything else is going to get reduced."
Clinton administration and congressional negotiators are trying to work out a compromise cutting federal deficits to zero in 2002. The deficit last year was $107 billion.
